title: Byte-extraction's hand-rolled unescape has an incomplete Gleam escape table — silent-drift corner in an otherwise loud-failing coupling
detail: Decoder handles only \n \t \r \\ \" \/; Gleam \b \e \f \v \0 \u{...} would decode to wrong bytes without error, so the eval'd scrub could silently test bytes that differ from what ships.
recommended_fix: Fail loud on unknown escapes: map unhandled \\(.) pairs to a sentinel that breaks eval, or assert the extracted region contains only the known escape sequences before evaluating.
